quote: If a third party claims or threatens a claim that Materials or Base Components IBM provides to Customer or uses in connection with the performance of the Services infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret, then IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors against that claim
rationale: IBM gives a defend-and-indemnify IP infringement indemnity covering patent, trademark, copyright and trade secret, with the usual exclusions (our contributions, modifications, combinations, non-IBM items) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and indemnity payments are uncapped under § 9.1(a) — this sits at (indeed above) the fallback. Noted, not flagged: no indemnity for IBM's breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and our reverse indemnity at § 8.2(a)(3) for Services Recipient claims "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" is broader than our preferred narrow scope; we would raise both as secondary asks.

quote: Type I Materials are those, created during the Service performance period, in which Customer will have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright).
rationale: We own Type I Materials created for us, IBM retains its pre-existing Type II Materials but grants us an irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up licence, and there is no assignment of our Content or data to IBM and no joint ownership — this meets the fallback. Noted, not flagged: the Type II licence is limited to use within our US Enterprise with no modify/sublicense right, Materials default to Type II if unspecified, the licence-back to IBM over Type I Materials permits external distribution and derivative works, and there is no affirmative statement that we retain ownership of Content — points we would negotiate as secondary asks.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The caps are mutual and 12-months-of-charges based, which works for us, but our position requires carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud, and we cannot accept IBM excluding all liability for loss of our records or data in a hosting deal.

ops.newText: 2. loss of, or damage to, any other entity's records or data. The limitations in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 do not apply to either party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, or its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and IBM remains liable for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data.
ops.oldText: 2. loss of, or damage to, Customer's or any other entity's records or data.

proposal.summary: Add mutual carve-outs to the liability caps and remove the blanket exclusion of liability for loss of Customer data

quote: the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.
rationale: The caps are mutual and based on 12 months' charges (greater of $100,000), and indemnity payments and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the cap; consequential damages are mutually excluded with our payment obligations properly carved out. However, there is no carve-out for breach of confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM liability entirely for loss of or damage to our records or data in a hosting deal — that fails the fallback on carve-outs. Redline adds a mutual carve-out sentence and deletes the data-loss exclusion; indemnities and confidentiality must sit outside the cap.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition.
rationale: This sits at the fallback: we may assign to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition without consent, other assignments need consent that cannot be unreasonably withheld, and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right for IBM. Noted, not flagged: no express affiliate carve-out for us and no restriction on IBM's own assignment (IBM may also subcontract under § 14.8) — asks we would raise if the draft reopens.

quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
rationale: There is no exclusivity, sole-supplier or "all requirements" obligation on us; charges are for Services ordered under Order Forms and § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. We remain free to buy from other suppliers.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Early termination charges set solely by Attachment A are open-ended; our position is no liquidated amounts payable by us, with a fallback of a single early-termination fee capped at three months' charges.

ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services and will be the only amounts payable by Customer as a result of such termination.
ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

proposal.summary: Cap the early termination charges payable by Customer at three months' charges

quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
rationale: Our convenience exit is conditioned on open-ended early termination charges set entirely by Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no cap in the Base Terms — a Customer-payable liquidated amount of unknown size. Redline caps those charges at three months' charges for the terminated Services as the sole amount payable on termination (our fallback); we credit that § 3.3 already disapplies them where IBM is the breaching party and that ordinary late-payment fees under § 4.2 are acceptable.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A licence revocable at IBM's discretion, with no coverage for our Affiliates or contractors, is a walk-away for us; the licence should run for the term and be terminable only in accordance with Section 3.3.

ops.newText: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement, which license IBM may not revoke except upon termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 3.
ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Remove the at-will revocability of the Base Components licence and extend it to Affiliates and contractors

quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
rationale: The Base Components licence is expressly revocable, is limited to us alone (no Affiliates or contractors, with § 14.17 confirming no other rights are granted, unlike the Type II Materials licence which covers our Enterprise) and offers no path to add them — squarely our walk-away case. Redline deletes "revocable", ties termination of the licence to Section 3, and extends it to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf.

quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; § 14.16 expressly preserves each party's freedom of action. The only restriction on our activities is the § 14.11 bar on reselling the Services, which is a scope-of-use limit rather than a restraint on our business lines and does not engage this rule.

quote: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
rationale: We hold a convenience termination right on one month's notice (better than our preferred 30 days), IBM must continue performing through the final termination date, and IBM has no convenience right at all — only termination for uncured material breach under § 3.3. Noted, not flagged here: the early termination charges referenced in Attachment A are unquantified; we address capping them under the LD rule to avoid duplicating the same commercial ask.

quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
rationale: There is no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against us and no right of access to our systems or premises; § 11.3 is only an acceptable-use investigation right, exercisable on reasonable-efforts prior notice before restricting access or removing Content. The absence of Customer-facing audit rights matches our preferred position, so nothing to redline.

quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
rationale: New York law is our preferred governing law and there is no arbitration clause or foreign venue. Noted, not flagged: no express exclusive venue in New York County (we would add it if the draft reopens), and § 14.14 imposes a two-year contractual limitations period, which is a separate point outside this rule.

quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms.
rationale: No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation runs against us anywhere in the pricing terms; pricing is set by Service Option Attachments and Order Forms, with IBM price changes only after 12 months on 90 days' notice and a fee-free exit if we disagree (§ 13.1). Nothing to redline.

quote: Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage.
rationale: The Base Terms contain no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction (searches for "minimum", "commit" and "shortfall" return nothing); charges are for Services ordered, and § 11.5 places capacity planning with us without committing volumes. Any commitment would have to appear in an Order Form or Service Option Attachment, and our § 3.4 one-month convenience exit applies — we will confirm the Attachment A/Order Form terms when provided.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: Each party is responsible for the supervision, direction, and control of its respective personnel. IBM reserves the right to determine the assignment of its personnel.
rationale: Section 14.8 (Personnel) contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or inducement restriction, and a document-wide search for "solicit" returns nothing. This matches our preferred position of no non-solicit binding us.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Renewal terms that mirror a multi-year initial term with a 90-day exit window are outside our position; we need 12-month renewals with a 30-day (fallback 60-day) non-renewal notice.

ops.newText: for an additional term of twelve (12) months
ops.oldText: for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment

ops.newText: at least thirty (30) days prior to the end
ops.oldText: at least ninety (90) days prior to the end

proposal.summary: Fix renewal term at 12 months and shorten the non-renewal notice window to 30 days

quote: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term
rationale: The 90-day non-renewal window exceeds our fallback of 60 days, and renewal for a term "equal in duration to the previous term" produces automatic multi-year renewals where an Order Form term is multi-year — walk-away territory. Redline fixes renewals at 12 months and shortens the notice window to 30 days; uncapped renewal pricing is mitigated by the § 13.1 fee-free exit on price change, so we note rather than redline uplift.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.5 addresses only our payment obligations; we need transition assistance and return of our Content in a machine-readable format, followed by certified deletion.

ops.text: Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM will (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return all Content and other Customer data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and deletion obligations on termination

quote: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable.
rationale: Section 3.5 deals only with our payment obligations; nothing in the Agreement requires IBM to provide transition assistance, return our Content in a usable format, or delete it afterwards (the only "return" obligation runs against us, for Materials, under § 8.1). For a hosting agreement that is a material gap. Redline inserts a transition-assistance, data-return-within-30-days and certified-deletion paragraph into § 3.5, which already survives termination under § 14.2.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM warrants only reasonable care and skill, with Materials provided "AS IS" and no remedy; we need at least a 90-day conformance warranty for deliverables with re-performance, repair or refund, carved out of Sections 5.2 and 5.4.

ops.text: IBM further warrants that, for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Materials deliverable and the Base Components will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation and Service Option Attachments. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services, Materials or Base Components. The warranties in this Section 5.1 are not limited or disclaimed by Sections 5.2 or 5.4.

proposal.summary: Add a conformance warranty for Materials and Base Components with a re-performance/refund remedy, carved out of the disclaimers

quote: IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND
rationale: IBM warrants only reasonable care and skill plus compliance with laws applicable to its own business; there is no conformance warranty for Materials or Base Components (they are supplied "AS IS"), no warranty period and no stated remedy, and §§ 5.2/5.4 disclaim everything else including capacity, performance and secure operation. That fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace or refund). Redline adds a 90-day conformance warranty with a re-performance/repair/refund remedy and carves the express warranties out of the disclaimers.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no insurance obligation even though IBM hosts our environment and processes our data; we require standard CGL, E&O and cyber coverage with certificates on request.

ops.text: 14.12A Insurance. IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. IBM shall provide certificates of insurance on Customer's request.

proposal.summary: Insert a Vendor insurance covenant in the general terms

quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
rationale: No insurance obligation exists anywhere in the Agreement (a search for "insurance" returns nothing); § 14.12 allocates risk of loss but requires no coverage. For a vendor hosting our environment and processing personal data on our behalf (§ 14.18), that is our walk-away case. Redline inserts a short insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp) with certificates on request in the general terms.
